title: Review: Sol fifth pass after lifecycle consolidation
description:
READ-ONLY REVIEW. Do not edit, create, or delete any file; do not commit; do not push. Your only writes are bd notes on this bead and closing it.

SCOPE: the full diff of branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 against origin/main (`git diff origin/main...HEAD`) — one PR carrying eight beads: eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.4 (character suffocation recovery gate, migration 0032, set_suffocation, calc breath formulas), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.5 (player-character death rules for encounter combatants, migration 0033), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.6 (adjust_hp knockOut), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.3 (adjust_exhaustion, derived level-4 HP maximum, level-6 death), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.11.4 (expend_ammunition / recover_ammunition, migration 0034), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.10.3 (roll_retained_check / resolve_retained_check / end_retained_check, set_surprised derived from comparisons, migration 0035), eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.6 (hydra Multiple Heads curated mechanic, tracked head count, derived reaction allowance, migration 0036), eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.5 (action:use-an-object ordinaryInteractionRuleRef -> rule:other-activity-on-your-turn, importer). Run `bd show` on each bead and on eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 for the specs and acceptance criteria.

AUTHORITY: AGENTS.md; docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md (profile rules-clause-complete); ADR 0020 §§2-3 (dice, arithmetic, atomic state mutation, resource accounting, state integrity are deterministic; adjudicated outcomes still pass through those boundaries); docs/design/rule-record-runtime-statements.md amendments A3-A5 and invariants 12-13; ADR 0015 (migration-first schema); docs/importer-fix-protocol.md for the importer parts; the committed SRD source text for every rule (packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json, records use the `key` field).

METHOD (review the mechanism, not the narrative):
1. For each capability, print the governing SRD source text beside the implementation and check source fidelity of every engine rule (thresholds, tie semantics, rounding, ordering, what counts as damage/healing, lifecycle start/end).
2. Check every model-facing surface (tool descriptions, schemas, Hybrid Contract in protocol.ts, known-limit statements in ruleKnownLimits.ts, error/rejection messages) against the real code: truthful, no model-side arithmetic/comparison or model-held canonical state offered as a fallback, target domain correct (character vs combatant), no stale wording from the pre-capability disclosures.
3. State integrity: atomicity (single transaction), invariants across the full state space (alive/dying/stable/dead, monster vs player-character rules, recovery block, exhaustion levels, closed vs active combat instances, missing/malformed rows), concentration and attunement side effects, campaign-actor sync, provenance conventions, deterministic ids/replay, write paths that bypass established helpers (mutateState, claimItem, removeItem), migration correctness (constraints, indexes, data preservation, contiguity, schema snapshot).
4. Write paths that let a model persist an unsupported/derived value (the A5 forbidden-substitution class), and any place a refusal could be bypassed through another tool (e.g. add_condition, update_combatant status, rest, level-up).
5. Test evidence: does each acceptance criterion have a test that distinguishes the bad state from the good state? Name missing evidence only where a real requirement is unprotected.
6. Sibling search: for each defect, look for the same class elsewhere in the diff.

REPORT with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes`, then `bd close <this bead>`. One entry per finding: ID (S1, S2, ...), severity (blocker / should-fix / nit), file:line, the violated requirement and its authority, a concrete failure scenario (inputs -> wrong state), and the minimal fix. Then a short list of what you checked and found correct. Apply the review policy's "From observation to finding" test: an observation without an operative requirement is "no requirement" in one line, not a finding. Do not stop at the first defect; batch everything you can find.

FIFTH PASS — FRESH FULL REVIEW AFTER DESIGN CONSOLIDATION. Prior Sol reviews: eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.1, .8.4, .8.6, .8.8 (read all). Since .8.8 the supervisor replaced per-path lifecycle repairs with a design consolidation, batch E (bead eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.10, read its description D1-D9 and notes): a pure nextCombatantLifecycle transition function (state/combatantLifecycle.ts) routed through every combatant/actor writer, single recovery-schedule owner, settled-state rules, actor invariants without the lifecycle subtree, resolver threading, ammunition identity snapshot (migration 0038), and a state-aware sequence test. The branch also merged origin/main (PR #597). (1) State CLOSED/OPEN for S3, S4, S14, S19, S20, S22, S23, S24, S25, S26 with fresh adversarial evidence. (2) Review the consolidation itself: is the transition function complete and correct against the source for every event, is every writer (grep every UPDATE/INSERT of encounter_combatant, campaign_actor, character HP/life columns) actually routed through it or an equivalent validated path, and does the sequence test reach every event class with checked outcomes? (3) Fresh full review of the rest of the PR (IDs from S27). Apply "From observation to finding" strictly. Close with APPROVE-READY or CHANGES REQUESTED.
acceptance_criteria: Closure states plus any new findings recorded in bd notes with an overall disposition; no file changes; bead closed by the reviewer.

Review bound to HEAD d4bcc88a10b66b3bac47226c378172b9a20e7d29, origin/main ae84049831f4c3836d24c6a289cb2f63bdbead0f; rules-clause-complete. Live scope, capability, prior-review and batch-E beads read; refs/beads/state is stale (2026-09-09), so live Beads supplies current authority.

S27 | blocker | packages/core/src/state/combatantLifecycle.ts:592
Requirement/authority: creature:hydra Multiple Heads regains ten HP per regrown head at own-turn end; rule:healing resets death saves on HP regain; .19.3.4.6 and batch-E D1 require complete source-correct transitions, including skipped dying turns (previous S13). ADR 0020 owns HP/lifecycle atomically.
Failure through registered tools: PC-rules hydra172/172 -> update_combatant(hpDelta:-172), leaving dying0HP/four heads/one pending loss -> begin_turn(hydra). Eligible regrowth adds20HP but only stable, not dying, is changed to alive, so final validation refuses dying at positiveHP and rolls back the entire turn. Fire-suppressed sibling succeeds; recovery-blocked sibling is checked separately. The helper also leaves earned death-save counters untouched when regrowth actually heals.
Minimal fix: run eligible regrowth HP gain through the same actual-positive-regain lifecycle transition as ordinary healing, for both dying and stable states; reset both counters and recovery facts, preserve blocked zero-regain head settlement and fire/dead exclusions.
Permanent evidence: generalized own-turn settlement matrix over dying/stable/alive/dead, block/fire and positive/zero regain with nonzero dying counters; assert successful boundary, HP/status/counters, heads and actor parity. Owner: lifecycle/head integration. Material repair; required next state: fix before approval and fresh affected-mechanism review.

S28 | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/combatantLifecycle.ts:365
Requirement/authority: .19.5.7.4 requires blocked death saves to remain recordable without stabilization/HP regain, .19.5.7.5 requires character parity; batch-E D1 requires invariant-valid complete state. SRD rule:suffocating and rule:death-saving-throws; persisted counters are constrained0..3.
Failure through registry: PC-rules goblin20/20 -> set_suffocation(drop) -> four record_death_save(roll:12). First three succeed and leave dying/suffocating/successes3; fourth attempts successes4 and fails the SQL CHECK constraint, rolling back. Fifth repeats the error. Character resolveDeathSaveTransition and the combatant natural20 branch already cap successes at3; the ordinary-success branch does not.
Minimal fix: cap successful counter accumulation at3 while recovery remains blocked, keeping failures and breathing-trigger stabilization intact.
Permanent evidence: generalized gated death-save sequence across both domains and ordinary-success/natural20 mixtures beyond three successes, then failure and breathe transitions; proportionate to this bounded tool failure. Owner: suffocation/death-save integration. Material behavioral repair; required next state: repair before approval.
Location correction: S27 points to combatantLifecycle.ts:586 (headsRegrown life-state branch); S28 points to combatantLifecycle.ts:393 (uncapped ordinary-success accumulation).

S29 | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:2548; packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolUpdateCombatant.ts:40
Requirement/authority: .19.5.7.5 explicitly preserves default monster behavior; the existing update_combatant contract and SRD rule:knocking-a-creature-out support a nonlethal monster knockout by damage plus status:unconscious. Batch-E D1 must preserve supported event paths; ADR0020 owns atomic state application.
Failure through registry: default monster-rules goblin20/20 -> update_combatant(hpDelta:-20,status:unconscious) now refuses dead combatant cannot change status, rolling back HP to20. Consolidation applies ordinary damage first (deriving dead), then applies the requested status as a forbidden revival. The registered description still explicitly directs this exact knockout call. status:stable is also refused for monster rules, so the documented default knockout path is lost. PC-rules status:stable succeeds and remains distinct from arbitrary participation overrides.
Minimal fix: recognize the authorized monster nonlethal knockout before ordinary lethal damage, preserve its existing unconscious result (or explicitly authorize and implement a replacement), and keep terminal exhaustion/zero-head and post-death guards. Reconcile description with actual accepted behavior.
Permanent evidence: generalized default-monster/PC knockout boundary for below-zero/overflow damage, ordinary lethal damage and terminal causes, asserting success and HP/status plus no revival bypass. Owner: combatant lifecycle integration. Material behavioral repair; required next state: repair before approval.
S25 | OPEN (alternate effect producer repaired; standalone actor write gate incomplete) | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:1417, :1463
Requirement/authority: batch-E D6 explicitly requires campaign_actor writes to enforce I1/I6 even without combatLifecycle; ADR0020 state integrity and atomic mutation. The retained actor upsert write boundary is implementation required by that decision, including pretracking actors.
Fresh boundary probe: upsert a legacy-shaped actor alive20/20/state:{}; call upsertCampaignActor with conditions:[exhaustion6]. It throws I1, but a subsequent getCampaignActor returns the committed actor alive20/20/exhaustion6. The level4 sibling throws I6 and still leaves committed HP20/effectiveMax10. Validation runs after the autocommitted INSERT/UPSERT. The new permanent test asserts only that an exception is thrown, so it passes with this corrupt state. Inspected every production caller: current callers normally supply an enclosing transaction, so the live model start_effect bypass from S25 is repaired; severity reflects the lower-consequence standalone internal boundary rather than claiming those protected callers currently commit corruption.
Minimal fix: validate the candidate actor and terminal transition before issuing SQL, or give the required write boundary its own withTransaction so failed validation restores the previous actor, including when called directly. Audit ensureCampaignActorFromCombatant for the same standalone assumption.
Permanent evidence: one generalized actor admission/update rejection invariant, absent/present combatLifecycle and exhaustion4/6, checking stored rows remain unchanged after the error; extend the existing D6 regression rather than add duplicative fixtures. Owner: actor lifecycle integration. Material state-integrity repair; required next state: enforce the accepted gate before approval.

S30 | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:2448
Requirement/authority: batch-E D1 requires source-correct effective-max/clamp transitions, updateCombatant supports the internal hpMax input, and ADR0020 owns HP arithmetic. The effective maximum must derive from the resulting base maximum and conditions.
Fresh supported internal-boundary calls: goblin20/20 -> updateCombatant(hpMax:30,hpDelta:10) succeeds but persists20/30 rather than30/30. The transition passes newHpMax30 with newEffectiveHpMax computed from current.hpMax20, so healing remains capped at the obsolete maximum. Lowering hpMax to10 refuses I6 and rolls back rather than doing the prescribed non-damage clamp. Siblings vary exhaustion4 and settled effectiveMax0->positive rearm. This hpMax input has no current model-tool exposure; severity and evidence are bounded to the retained internal mutation seam.
Minimal fix: compute nextEffectiveMax from baseHpMax (the input-or-current resulting maximum) and resulting conditions, then use that fact consistently for clamp, healing and settled-state rearm.
Permanent evidence: a small generalized base-maximum change boundary over increase/decrease, exhaustion below/above4 and settled zero->positive maximum, asserting HP/max/lifecycle and preserved damage/head/temp accounting. Owner: combatant lifecycle integration. Localized material behavior repair; required next state: repair before approval.
S31 | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:561
Requirement/authority: batch-E D1 routes begin_turn resets through the complete lifecycle transition; D9 requires actor/projection parity after every operation; durable actor sync and ADR0020 own state/identity integrity. A transition that repairs HP or life state must commit its dependent canonical actor state as one result.
Fresh deliberately historical/malformed-state probe (not a claim that begin_turn creates the input): seed a recurring goblin projection and actor alive12/12 with exhaustion6, as old pre-capability state can contain. Registered begin_turn(character:pc-1) succeeds and repairs the projection to dead6HP/exhaustion6, but resetCombatantDamageForTurn never syncs the actor; it remains alive12HP/exhaustion6. The same result occurs when only the projection is inconsistent. The new begin-turn repair regression checks only the row, missing canonical parity. Ordinary accumulator-only resets need no actor change, but the pure transition now also derives mandatory terminal causes.
Sibling search: other persistCombatantLifecycle event writers synchronize current actor projections; historical invalidation deliberately must not sync. This reset path is the uncovered repair producer. Reachability/consequence is lower for this historical-state repair than an ordinary model mutation; severity reflects that.
Minimal fix: apply resulting HP/life-state side effects and sync the current actor when reset produces such a repair, in beginTurns existing transaction (or refuse the unsupported state atomically instead of committing divergent canonical owners). Preserve normal accumulator reset and historical schedule ownership.
Permanent evidence: extend the existing begin-turn repair test into a generalized actor/projection parity boundary with exhaustion6 and ordinary rows, asserting both owners after success and unchanged state on refusal. Owner: lifecycle reset/actor integration. Material state-integrity repair; required next state: repair before approval.

S32 | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:3156, :2354; packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolEndEffect.ts:76
Requirement/authority: the exact campaign-bound resolver contract, ADR0020 bounded provider-neutral execution and state integrity, and existing F3 start_effect/end_effect contracts require condition projections and cleanup to operate on the same available bound rules stack. This PR adds unconditional creature/mechanic lookup to updateCombatant, so its real producer set must carry the resolver.
Fresh registered probes with installLateAmbiguityAddon and its resolver on ToolContext: start_encounter succeeds, but start_effect(condition-package, source:ruling, condition:incapacitated) targeting either a COMBATANT or its active CAMPAIGN_ACTOR fails unavailable add-on. The nested updateCombatant calls omit the resolver; updateCampaignActor has no resolver input. Sibling: create that condition effect before installing the add-on, install it, then end_effect(reason:ruled) with the available resolver. It likewise refuses and rolls back, leaving the effect/condition active. The source record and installed stack are available; ordinary update_combatant, repaired set_surprised and adjust_exhaustion succeed on that same stack. Incapacitated uses the existing name shortcut, so the newly unconditional head-mechanic lookup is sufficient to introduce this failure even where the old condition check needed no resolver.
Minimal fix: thread the exact resolver through the condition projection/removal and actor mutation producer paths, including end/expiry/concentration cleanup where those paths call updateCombatant; preserve rollback on genuinely unavailable bindings. Do not bypass exact stack resolution or return missing as a substitute for failed cleanup.
Permanent evidence: generalized available/unavailable installed-stack parity through actual effect creation AND cleanup, with combatant/active-actor targets; assert successful state/effect mutation when available and atomic refusal otherwise. Owner: combatant/F3 resolver integration. Material consumer-wiring repair; required next state: repair before approval.

Requirement/authority: batch-E D5 explicitly requires an exhaustion change that raises a settled stable creatures effective maximum above0 to re-arm a fresh1d4-hour recovery. rule:stabilizing-a-creature requires unhealed stable recovery; ADR0020 owns its schedule. remove_condition is an existing registered supported full-condition removal, so it is part of the exhaustion write blast radius.

Combatant sibling update_combatant(removeCondition:exhaustion) correctly re-arms and recovers1HP on the next due advance; adjust_exhaustion(delta:-4) likewise works for characters.
Minimal fix: route supported character exhaustion removal through the same canonical exhaustion/lifecycle rearm seam (or explicitly refuse it in favor of adjust_exhaustion), preserving full removal semantics where authorized. Audit long-rest/direct condition reduction siblings against the same settled-state transition.
Permanent evidence: generalized settled recovery continuity across exhaustion mutation producers (adjust_exhaustion and existing removal path), character/combatant parity, and zero->positive/remaining-zero maxima; assert stored schedule then actual due recovery. Owner: character exhaustion/recovery integration. Material behavior repair; required next state: repair before approval.

S34 | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/combatantLifecycle.ts:380; packages/core/src/state/hpLifecycle.ts:776
Requirement/authority: committed rule:death-saving-throws says a roll10 or higher succeeds and the third success makes the creature stable, resetting both counters. Suffocation forbids stabilization only while recovery_block is present; condition:exhaustion level4 halves the HP maximum, not stabilization. .19.5.7.3/.19.5.7.5 and batch-E D1 require source-correct zero-maximum lifecycle and character/combatant parity; ADR0020 owns the result and schedule.

The natural20 zero-regain branch increments the counter and exits without applying the ordinary third-success stabilization. Another bad save can now kill a creature that should already be stable. Siblings:12,12,12 at zero maximum correctly stabilizes in both domains; with suffocation set, both last12 and last20 correctly stay dying with successes3. Positive-maximum natural20 revival remains separately correct.
Minimal fix: when natural20 cannot actually regain HP, apply the same capped success and unblocked third-success stabilization logic as ordinary successes; preserve suffocation blocking and successful positive-HP revival, and arm the ordinary zero-maximum recovery schedule.
Permanent evidence: a compact generalized third-success boundary varying last ordinary/natural20, zero/positive effective maximum, recovery block and both domains; assert status/counters/schedule and ensuing recovery settlement. This is source-backed durable lifecycle behavior, proportionate to the existing table/sequence evidence. Owner: shared character/combatant death-save transition.
